used_cases.flag: an actionable space is not an outcome
trust decay cannot be rebuilt on demand
naming the Solomon Paradox does not exempt you from it
the framework finds the 18th camel but not who pays for it
structural conflict of interest between institution and principals: WHO cannot act at pathogen speed against its largest funders
absence of political will may be structural: governments that need the conflict may be unable to afford the 18th camel
when the powerful and the responsible are the same population, crisis communication is not a technical problem
the gap is not informational — who is constituted as an expert in their own risk environment is answered by power before principled analysis
principled pragmatism has no position when the diagnostic role itself has no political standing
analytical frameworks, once institutionalized, acquire a political life independent of their accuracy — revision requires simultaneously saying 'I was wrong,' which no protocol makes safe

when professional liability is diffuse enough that each actor assumes someone else verified the critical condition, no individual has to be negligent for the system to fail — the architecture of accountability itself is the problem

there is a class of public health crisis where the intervention's effectiveness depends on relational legitimacy that runs slower than the epidemic — principled pragmatism can name the co-design pathway but cannot compress the time required to earn the trust
